tools.definition: Fast decay adapts quickly but forgets; slow decay is stable but reacts late to a changed situation.

tools.title: Interpreter (virtual machine)

transform.reason: Virtual execution needs instructions, machine state, host calls, and yield semantics.

tools.definition: Executes the instruction stream with a stack or registers, calling into the engine through bound functions and supporting yield for re-entrancy.

verified.note: model-knowledge (unnumbered in 3e TOC; named in assignment list)

tools.title: Tables (symbol and function binding)
tools.definition: Lookups from names to variables, functions and engine hooks that the compiler and interpreter share.

verified.note: model-knowledge (unnumbered in 3e TOC; named in assignment list)

tools.title: Rolling your own as an anti-pattern
tools.definition: The chapter's verdict: a custom language costs far more than expected in tooling, debugging and maintenance, and an embedded existing language almost always wins.

hooks.clause: prefer an existing format or language to inventing a project-specific one

tools.title: Designing game AI
tools.definition: How to go from a game design to an AI design: list the behaviours players should see, judge them, pick the simplest techniques, then apply the recipe genre by genre.

tools.title: The design (behaviour-first process)

transform.reason: Behaviour-first design needs a visible-behaviour brief and technique-selection criteria.

tools.definition: Start from the behaviours each character type must show, not from techniques; the techniques are chosen last to serve the visible behaviour.

hooks.clause: plan from observable outcomes, choose mechanisms last

tools.title: Worked example
tools.definition: A sample character brief (patrolling, noticing, investigating, raising alarm, fighting) used to show how the behaviour list is drawn up.

tools.title: Evaluating the behaviours

transform.reason: Behaviour ranking needs visibility, value, and cost estimates plus a decision rule.

tools.definition: Rate each listed behaviour by how often the player will see it, how much it matters to the game and what it would cost, so effort follows visibility.

hooks.clause: spend scrutiny where the operator will actually see the result

tools.title: Selecting techniques

transform.reason: Technique selection needs behaviour requirements and evidence of technique sufficiency.

tools.definition: Map each behaviour to the simplest technique that produces it, reusing one technique for several behaviours where possible, and resist exotic methods.

hooks.clause: pick the simplest mechanism that produces the required observable

tools.title: The scope of one game
tools.definition: Design for the game in hand rather than a general AI engine; generality is earned across projects, not built up front.

hooks.clause: let the kit generalise from instances rather than designing the general case first

tools.title: Shooter AI

transform.reason: A shooter scene needs aiming, damage, alert-state, and perception contracts.

tools.definition: The genre's stack: movement and aiming, alert-level decision making, modelled perception, navigation with cover, and variants for stealth and melee.

tools.title: A structure for tactical analyses

transform.reason: A common analysis interface needs cache, scheduling, and composition contracts.

tools.definition: Model every analysis as a map over the same location set with a shared interface, so analyses can be combined arithmetically, cached and updated on their own schedules.

hooks.clause: one shape for all projections so they compose

tools.title: Movement and firing

transform.reason: Movement and firing need aim control, weapon effects, reaction timing, and animation coupling.

tools.definition: Steering tied to animation, aiming with deliberate inaccuracy and reaction delay, weapon choice, and the rule that the AI must be beatable and readable.

tools.title: Decision making (shooters)

transform.reason: Alert-state decisions need a state graph, perception inputs, and transition actions.

tools.definition: Mostly state machines or behaviour trees over alert levels (idle, suspicious, alert, combat) with transitions driven by perception.

tools.title: Perception (shooters)

transform.reason: Shooter perception needs geometric sensing and player-readable detection rules.

tools.definition: Sight cones, hearing and line-of-sight checks, usually simplified, with the stealth variants needing honest sense management so the player can predict detection.

hooks.clause: detection rules an operator can predict beat accurate ones they cannot

tools.title: Pathfinding and tactical AI (shooters)

transform.reason: Tactical navigation needs cover queries, route execution, and a squad protocol.

tools.definition: Navigation meshes or waypoint graphs, cover points and tactical waypoints, with squad coordination for groups.

tools.title: Shooter-like games

transform.reason: Genre variants need concrete stealth, survival, or action objectives and mechanics.

tools.definition: Third-person action, stealth and survival horror reuse the stack with shifted emphasis, such as perception and tension in stealth.

tools.title: Melee combat

transform.reason: Melee needs attack windows, defence rules, animation state, and spacing control.

tools.definition: Close-quarters fighting AI: spacing and positioning, attack and defence timing against the player's rhythm, animation-driven moves and prediction of the player's patterns.

tools.title: Driving AI

transform.reason: Driving needs a vehicle state, track, collision model, and control interface.

tools.definition: Vehicles follow a racing line with physics-aware control, overtake and block, and the model stretches to flight, boats and other steerable craft.

tools.title: Movement (driving)

transform.reason: Vehicle control needs dynamics and throttle-brake-steering feedback operations.

tools.definition: Control throttle, brake and steering to follow a target line under vehicle physics, with look-ahead and corrective feedback rather than direct position setting.

tools.title: Racing line
tools.definition: The precomputed or authored ideal path around a track, often with speed targets per segment, that driving AI steers toward.

tools.title: Pathfinding and tactical AI (driving)

transform.reason: Driving tactics need vehicle interactions, overtaking goals, and recovery controllers.

tools.definition: Overtaking, blocking, avoiding collisions and recovering from spins; open-world driving adds road-network pathfinding.

tools.title: Composite (derived) analysis

transform.reason: Derived fields need a defined expression, input maps, and scale normalization.

tools.definition: Build a new map by combining existing ones per location, e.g. multiply friendly security by visibility to rate sniping spots, or subtract danger from control to rate safe advances.

tools.title: Difficulty balancing (rubber-banding)

transform.reason: Race balancing needs an explicit handicap mechanism and player-relative progress state.

tools.definition: Keeping AI racers near the player keeps races tense but reads as cheating when overt; the design chooses how visible the help is.

tools.title: Driving-like games

transform.reason: Other craft need their own physics, control constraints, and travel surfaces.

tools.definition: Flight, boats, hovercraft and similar: the same control-and-line model with different physics and degrees of freedom.

tools.title: Real-time strategy AI

transform.reason: Strategy scenes need economy, construction, multi-unit command, and opponent state.

tools.definition: Many units, a map and an economy: pathfinding at scale, group movement, map-level tactical analysis, strategic decision making, and the MOBA variant.

tools.title: Pathfinding (RTS)

transform.reason: Shared navigation needs route caching, hierarchical search, and crowd-resolution rules.

tools.definition: Hundreds of units need hierarchical or shared pathfinding, path reuse and handling of crowds at chokepoints.

tools.title: Group movement
tools.definition: Formations and steering keep units together on the move and arriving coherently, with slot assignment and speed matching.

tools.title: Tactical and strategic AI (RTS)

transform.reason: Map-level strategy needs field interpretation and an objective-selection policy.

tools.definition: Influence maps and terrain analysis for where to fight, plus strategic layers for expansion, defence and timing of attacks.

tools.title: Decision making (RTS)

transform.reason: Economic decisions need resources, construction actions, and build-goal evaluation.

tools.definition: Economy and build decisions (what to build, when to expand, which technology) through rule systems, goal-based reasoning or scripted build orders.

tools.title: Build order
tools.definition: A scripted or planned sequence of early construction and research decisions, the RTS equivalent of an opening book.

hooks.clause: canonical opening sequences for a new order or instance

tools.title: MOBAs

transform.reason: Hero-team play needs abilities, lanes, objectives, and human-team coordination rules.

tools.definition: Hero-based team games: few units with many abilities, lane and objective strategy, and bots that must fill team roles and coordinate with human players.

tools.title: Sports AI

transform.reason: Sports scenes need ball physics, team roles, and scoring rules.

tools.definition: Predicting physics for interception and timing, and expressing team tactics as authored playbooks.

tools.title: Analysis update policy

transform.reason: Refresh policies need a field scheduler and explicit freshness or invalidation rules.

tools.definition: Static analyses compute once; dynamic ones refresh periodically or on demand; the policy per analysis balances freshness against frame budget.

tools.title: Physics prediction

transform.reason: Interception needs a motion model, forward prediction, and reachability timing.

tools.definition: Extrapolate projectile and body motion forward (closed form or stepwise) to decide where to be and when to act, as in catching or intercepting a ball.

hooks.clause: forecast when a running step will land to schedule the next dispatch

tools.title: Playbooks and content creation

transform.reason: Playbooks need authored roles, position targets, triggers, and coordinated execution.

tools.definition: Team tactics as designer-authored plays with roles, positions and triggers, produced with tools rather than coded, and selected at run time by situation.

hooks.clause: standard order templates with roles, authored as data and selected by situation

tools.title: Turn-based strategy game AI

transform.reason: Turn-based strategy needs legal actions, turn progression, and player-assistance contracts.

tools.definition: The AI must think within acceptable turn times and may also serve the player as an assistant.

tools.title: Timing (turn length)

transform.reason: Thinking limits need resumable decision work and a turn-time budget controller.

tools.definition: Bound the AI's thinking per turn, spread it across frames or the player's own turn, and hide the wait behind animation and feedback so it feels short.

hooks.clause: show progress during waits and use operator time for pre-computation

tools.title: Helping the player

transform.reason: Advising needs ranked suggestions, automation boundaries, and player-choice handling.

tools.definition: Use the same AI on the player's side: advisors, automation of tedious moves, suggestions and warnings, tuned so the player stays in charge.

hooks.clause: the resident as an advisor that automates tedium and never takes the decision

tools.title: AI-based game genres
tools.definition: Genres where the AI is the game itself rather than a supporting layer: creatures the player teaches, and flocks the player herds.

tools.title: Teaching characters

transform.reason: Teaching scenes need understandable feedback, a learnable action set, and learner state.

tools.definition: Games in which the player trains a creature by feedback and example, so the learning method is the core mechanic and must be legible and safe.

tools.title: Representing actions
tools.definition: A discrete, nameable set of things the creature can do (often action-object pairs) that learning can attach to and the player can recognise.

hooks.clause: a bounded, named action vocabulary makes agent learning legible

tools.title: Representing the world
tools.definition: Objects with attributes form the observation the creature learns over; what is representable bounds what can be taught.

tools.title: Learning mechanism

transform.reason: Creature learning needs feedback interpretation, demonstrations, and policy updates.

tools.definition: Reinforcement from player reward and punishment, imitation of what the player does, and classifiers or networks that associate situations with actions.

tools.title: Analysis cache (tactical analysis server)

transform.reason: Shared analysis caching needs lookup, ownership, and invalidation behaviour.

tools.definition: A central component that owns the analyses, serves lookups to many characters and recomputes only what is stale or requested.

tools.title: Predictable mental models
tools.definition: The player must be able to form a working model of how the creature learns; learning that cannot be anticipated cannot be taught and feels random.

hooks.clause: operators need a legible model of how feedback rules change behaviour

tools.title: Pathological states

transform.reason: Degeneracy recovery needs detectable failure states, reset operations, and behaviour floors.

tools.definition: Learned creatures can lock into degenerate behaviour (doing nothing, obsessive loops, fear of everything); designs need bounds, resets and designer-imposed floors.

hooks.clause: an agent that learns to refuse everything or repeat one move needs the same floors

tools.title: Flocking and herding games

transform.reason: A herding game needs player influence, steering rules, and an explicit herd objective.

tools.definition: Games built on steering: the player influences creatures that move by flocking rules, so the steering parameters are the gameplay.

tools.title: Making the creatures
tools.definition: Compose each creature from steering behaviours (separation, cohesion, alignment, wander, flee the player) and give species their own parameter sets.

tools.title: Tuning steering for interactivity

transform.reason: Response timing needs a steering-response or delay update; weight blending alone is insufficient.

tools.definition: Adjust responsiveness so the player's influence is visible and controllable: reactions quick enough to feel causal, slow enough to be steerable.

tools.title: Steering behaviour stability

transform.reason: Stability needs specified damping, priority, or hysteresis updates and oscillation criteria.

tools.definition: Blended behaviours can oscillate, jitter or deadlock; damping, priorities and hysteresis keep flocks from vibrating or freezing.

hooks.clause: a dispatch loop that oscillates between two states needs damping

tools.title: Ecosystem design

transform.reason: Ecosystems need feeding, reproduction, death, resource flow, and stabilizing feedback rules.

tools.definition: Predators, prey, food and reproduction form a system whose populations can boom or crash; design for stability with limits and feedback rather than trusting emergence.

hooks.clause: instances, kit and orders form an ecosystem that needs balancing feedback, not just growth

tools.title: References — Books, Periodicals, Papers and Websites
tools.definition: The bibliography of written sources the chapters cite by number; the preview's chapter 1 shows numbered bracket citations resolving here.

tools.title: References — Games (ludography)
tools.definition: A separate list of the games cited in the text, by title, so examples can be traced to specific titles; the appendix the assignment asked to check for is this two-part References section.

related.title: References — Books, Periodicals, Papers and Websites

tools.title: Index
tools.definition: Back-of-book index; present in the contents, not mapped further.

tools.title: Map flooding
tools.definition: Spread each source's influence outward through connected locations with a Dijkstra-like frontier so that influence follows walkable routes and stops at walls rather than crossing them geometrically.

hooks.clause: propagate impact along real dependencies, not by proximity

tools.title: Flooding vs geometric distance

transform.reason: Comparing propagation methods requires both distance models and a cost measurement contract.

tools.definition: Flooding respects the level's connectivity and gives distance-to-nearest fields for free, but costs a graph traversal per source instead of a cheap distance formula.

tools.title: Tactical quality (property)
tools.definition: A named property a location may have for a character, e.g. cover point, sniper point, shadow or hiding spot, defensive position, exposed/dangerous spot, power-up access.

tools.title: Convolution filters
tools.definition: Pass a small kernel over a grid-based map, replacing each cell with a weighted sum of its neighbourhood; blurring spreads influence smoothly and cheaply.

tools.title: Gaussian blur as influence spread
tools.definition: A bell-shaped kernel applied once or repeatedly approximates distance decay for every source at once, in time independent of the number of units.

tools.title: Separable filter

transform.reason: A two-pass filter needs explicit kernel factorization and execution instrumentation.

tools.definition: Apply a two-dimensional kernel as two one-dimensional passes (rows then columns) to cut the cost from kernel area to kernel width.

tools.title: Boundary handling

transform.reason: Edge handling needs a boundary policy and neighbourhood-indexing contract.

tools.definition: Cells at the map edge lack neighbours; options include clamping, wrapping or treating the outside as zero, each biasing edge values differently.

tools.title: Cellular automata

transform.reason: Cell evolution needs a local transition table and a simulation-step operation.

tools.definition: Update every cell from a local rule over its neighbours' previous values, step after step; simple rules yield rich, spreading, often surprising patterns.

tools.title: Synchronous update with double buffer

transform.reason: Double buffering needs simultaneous update and state-swap operations.

tools.definition: Compute the next generation into a second grid from the current one so no cell sees a half-updated neighbour, then swap.

tools.title: Automata for spreading phenomena

transform.reason: Propagation needs a phenomenon-specific cell transition and time-step model.

tools.definition: Use automata to model things that propagate through the level over time, such as fire, flooding, crowd pressure or shifting control, feeding the result into other analyses.

tools.title: Emergent complexity caution

transform.reason: Controllability needs bounded outcome criteria and a specified emergent-rule model.

tools.definition: Automata and other emergent rules are hard to predict and tune; the chapter warns against relying on them where designers need controllable outcomes.

hooks.clause: emergent multi-agent behaviour needs the same controllability check

tools.title: Tactical pathfinding
tools.definition: Make routes tactically sensible by letting tactical information change the cost of moving through locations, so a path avoids danger or hugs cover without a separate planner.

tools.title: The cost function
tools.definition: Edge cost becomes distance plus weighted tactical terms (danger, exposure, lack of cover) read from the analyses, keeping costs positive so the search stays valid.

tools.title: Primitive and compound tactics

transform.reason: Combining waypoint properties requires a composition expression and a property evaluator.

tools.definition: Store a few primitive qualities per point and derive richer ones by combining them (a sniping spot is cover plus long sight lines), rather than storing every tactic separately.

tools.title: Tactic weights and concern blending
tools.definition: Each tactical concern gets a weight, often per character or personality, and the weighted concerns are blended into one cost; weights express how cautious or aggressive a route is.

hooks.clause: blend time, token and risk concerns into one dispatch cost with explicit weights

tools.title: Modifying the pathfinding heuristic

transform.reason: Heuristic tuning needs a search implementation and admissibility or quality measurements.

tools.definition: Inflated tactical costs make a plain distance heuristic weak (more nodes searched) while raising it risks inadmissibility and sub-optimal routes; the section weighs both.

tools.title: Tactical graphs for pathfinding
tools.definition: A graph whose nodes are tactical waypoints and whose edges carry tactical cost, searched alone or layered over the normal navigation graph.

related.title: Tactical waypoints vs the pathfinding graph

tools.title: Using tactical waypoints (cover-to-cover movement)

transform.reason: Cover-to-cover motion needs a waypoint queue, pause conditions, and route execution.

tools.definition: Route through a chain of chosen tactical points, pausing at each, so movement reads as deliberate bounding between covers rather than a straight dash.

tools.title: Coordinated action

transform.reason: Team coordination needs a chosen command, local-rule, or script protocol.

tools.definition: Making several characters act as a team: by a command hierarchy, by emergence from individual rules, or by authored group scripts.

tools.title: Multi-tier AI

transform.reason: Layered control needs ownership, inter-level interfaces, and update timing.

tools.definition: Stack decision makers: a strategic or squad tier decides goals and issues orders, individual tiers decide how to carry them out, and a movement tier executes; each tier owns its own time scale.

hooks.clause: a lead agent issues goals downward and receives evidence upward instead of micromanaging workers

tools.title: Orders down, information up

transform.reason: Bidirectional messages need payloads and a causal feedback rule before a level loop exists.

tools.definition: Communication in the hierarchy flows both ways: higher tiers pass goals or orders down, lower tiers report what they see and whether they can comply.

hooks.clause: verifier and reviewer report upward; the order never edits itself from below

tools.title: Orders as goals, not scripts

transform.reason: Goal orders need a payload schema and subordinate autonomy rules.

tools.definition: Issuing a goal leaves the individual free to adapt to local conditions; issuing exact actions is predictable but brittle when the situation changes.

hooks.clause: brief workers with goals and constraints, not keystrokes

tools.title: Hierarchy levels (strategic, squad, individual, movement)
tools.definition: The usual tiers in a game: whole-side strategy, group or squad tactics, individual character decisions, and steering; more levels add latency and plumbing.

tools.title: Emergent cooperation

transform.reason: Local cooperation needs concrete interaction predicates and action rules.

tools.definition: Give individuals simple situational rules (hold fire when a teammate crosses, move when a teammate covers, do not share a cover point) so team-like behaviour appears without a coordinator.

hooks.clause: parallel workers with good local rules versus an orchestrator

tools.title: Context-sensitive tactical qualities

transform.reason: Contextual cover needs enemy-relative geometry tests; no tactical-quality evaluator is supplied.

tools.definition: Many qualities only hold relative to the current situation (cover is cover from someone); the point stores the static part and the character evaluates the dynamic part against enemy positions.

tools.title: Emergence vs control

transform.reason: Comparing control styles needs explicit team controllers and outcome criteria.

tools.definition: Emergent teamwork is cheap and robust to surprises but unpredictable and hard to tune or debug; hierarchical or scripted control is the reverse.

tools.title: Scripting group actions

transform.reason: Group scripts need role schemas, step transitions, and coordinator execution.

tools.definition: Author a set piece (a room entry, a flanking move) as a sequence of steps with roles, run by a coordinator that assigns characters to roles and advances the steps.

tools.title: Role (slot) assignment

transform.reason: Role matching needs task requirements, unit capabilities, and an assignment objective.

tools.definition: Match available characters to the roles a group script needs, by suitability and position, like filling formation slots.

hooks.clause: assign roles by fit and availability rather than fixed identity

tools.title: Script preconditions and abort paths

transform.reason: Script recovery needs start predicates, failure signals, and abort transitions.

tools.definition: A group script states what must hold to start and what to do when a step fails or the situation changes, otherwise characters perform a plan the world has already invalidated.

hooks.clause: an order carries its preconditions and its stop conditions

tools.title: Military tactics as design source
tools.definition: Borrow real doctrine (bounding overwatch, flanking, suppression and covering fire, fire teams) as templates for group behaviour and scripts.

tools.title: Believability over realism
tools.definition: Tactics are tuned for what players read as competent and fun, not for military accuracy; realism is a source of ideas, not the goal.

tools.title: Learning in game AI
tools.definition: Behaviour that changes with experience, either during play or between sessions, covering parameter tuning, prediction of the player, learned decisions and neural approaches.

tools.title: Online vs offline learning

transform.reason: Online and offline learning need model-update timing and reproducible training state.

tools.definition: Online learning adapts during play and can respond to the individual player but is hard to test; offline learning happens in development or between sessions and ships a fixed, QA-able result.

hooks.clause: compile feedback rules offline between runs rather than mutating behaviour mid-dispatch

tools.title: Intra-behaviour learning

transform.reason: Intra-behaviour tuning needs named parameters, a score, and an update rule.

tools.definition: Learning that tunes the inside of one behaviour, such as the parameters of a steering or aiming routine, while the behaviour's role stays fixed.

tools.title: Inter-behaviour learning

transform.reason: Behaviour selection learning needs fixed actions, observations, and learning updates.

tools.definition: Learning which behaviour to perform in a situation, a far harder problem because the space of choices and consequences is open-ended.

tools.title: Fuzzy (graded) tactical values

transform.reason: Boolean and graded properties need a value representation and a combination rule.

tools.definition: Qualities can be Boolean flags or graded degrees; graded values let compound tactics blend smoothly but cost more to store and evaluate.

tools.title: A warning (learning is risky)
tools.definition: Learned behaviour is unpredictable, hard to reproduce and hard to test; it can learn to be dull or wrong, and players often do not notice it; use it where failure is cheap.

hooks.clause: adaptive agent behaviour needs the same reproducibility and test burden before it ships

tools.title: Over-learning (overfitting)

transform.reason: Overfitting control needs training partitions, validation criteria, and model complexity controls.

tools.definition: Fitting the specific examples seen, including their noise, so the learned behaviour fails on anything slightly different.

hooks.clause: a rule derived from one incident that generalises to nothing

tools.title: The zoo of learning algorithms
tools.definition: The field is a menagerie of techniques; the chapter picks the handful that have earned a place in games and sketches how the rest relate.

tools.title: The balance of effort

transform.reason: The effort comparison needs authoring costs, data costs, and a success target.

tools.definition: Getting a learning method to behave well often takes more tuning and data work than hand-authoring the behaviour; learning pays only where hand authoring cannot reach.

hooks.clause: cost the adaptive machinery against the plain rule before adopting it

tools.title: Parameter modification

transform.reason: Parameter search needs a specified behaviour, score evaluator, and search operator.

tools.definition: Treat a behaviour's numeric parameters as the thing to learn: search the parameter space for values that score best on some measure of success.

tools.title: The parameter landscape
tools.definition: Picture the score as a surface over parameter values, with peaks (good settings), valleys and local maxima that trap simple search.

hooks.clause: tuning budgets and effort levels is a landscape search with local optima

tools.title: Hill climbing

transform.reason: Hill climbing needs parameter-neighbour generation, scoring, and acceptance updates.

tools.definition: From the current parameters, try small changes in each direction and move to whichever scores better; repeat until no neighbour improves.

tools.title: Extensions to basic hill climbing

transform.reason: Search extensions need a base optimizer plus explicit momentum, step, or restart rules.

tools.definition: Remedies for the basic method's weaknesses: momentum to keep moving in a good direction, adaptive step resolution, and multiple trials from different starting points.

tools.title: Momentum

transform.reason: Momentum needs optimizer state and a parameter-step update operation.

tools.definition: Carry part of the previous step into the next so the search accelerates along consistent slopes and rolls through small bumps.

tools.title: Adaptive resolution (step size)

transform.reason: Adaptive steps need an improvement signal and a resolution-update operation.

tools.definition: Take large steps while improvement is easy and shrink the step as the search nears a peak, trading speed for precision over time.

tools.title: Tactical waypoints vs the pathfinding graph

transform.reason: Navigation and tactical points need an explicit correspondence and lookup contract.

tools.definition: Tactical points may be the pathfinding nodes themselves or a separate, sparser set; sharing saves memory, separating keeps each set fit for its purpose.

tools.title: Multiple trials (random restarts)

transform.reason: Random restarts need initialization sampling, independent trials, and best-result retention.

tools.definition: Run the climb from several random starting points and keep the best result, to reduce the chance of ending on a poor local maximum.

tools.title: Annealing (simulated annealing)

transform.reason: Annealing needs proposal generation, probabilistic acceptance, and temperature updates.

tools.definition: Sometimes accept a worse neighbour, with a probability that falls as a temperature parameter cools, so the search can escape local maxima early and settle late.

hooks.clause: allow an occasionally worse-looking step while the plan is young, none when it is converging

tools.title: Boltzmann acceptance probability

transform.reason: Acceptance probabilities need score deltas, temperature state, and stochastic decisions.

tools.definition: The rule that makes acceptance of a worse move depend on how much worse it is relative to the current temperature.

tools.title: Cooling schedule

transform.reason: Cooling needs an iteration clock, temperature state, and a schedule function.

tools.definition: How temperature decreases over iterations; too fast freezes in a poor optimum, too slow wastes evaluations.

tools.title: Action prediction

transform.reason: Action forecasting needs an action vocabulary, history, and prediction model.

tools.definition: Guess what the player will do next from what they did before, so the AI can pre-empt or counter it.

tools.title: Left or right (binary guessing)

transform.reason: Binary guessing needs a two-action input stream, predictor, and scoring protocol.

tools.definition: The simplest case: predict which of two options the player will pick; humans are poor at being random, which is what makes prediction work.

tools.title: Raw probability

transform.reason: Frequency prediction needs action counts and a prediction-emission operation.

tools.definition: Count how often each option has been chosen and predict the most frequent; ignores sequence and context.

tools.title: String matching

transform.reason: Sequence matching needs history indexing and a continuation-selection rule.

tools.definition: Find the player's most recent few actions earlier in the history and predict whatever followed them then.

tools.title: N-grams

transform.reason: Sequence counts need context storage, updates, and a continuation query.

tools.definition: Keep counts of every observed sequence of N actions; given the last N-1 actions, predict the continuation with the highest count.

hooks.clause: predict the operator's next dispatch from recent phrases to pre-stage work

tools.title: Window size

transform.reason: Window tuning needs a sequence predictor and sample-support measurements.

tools.definition: Longer windows capture more specific patterns but need far more observations before predictions are trustworthy; short windows learn fast but miss context.

tools.title: Using tactical locations

transform.reason: A waypoint consumer must specify whether it assigns a goal, evaluates a choice, or sends an order.

tools.definition: Ways a character consumes tactical points: as movement targets, as inputs to its decision maker, and as a shared vocabulary for group orders.

tools.title: Hierarchical N-grams

transform.reason: Hierarchical prediction needs multiple context tables and an explicit backoff rule.

tools.definition: Maintain N-grams of several sizes at once and answer from the largest window that has seen enough examples to be confident, falling back to smaller ones.

hooks.clause: answer from the most specific index that has enough support, else fall back

tools.title: Confidence threshold (minimum observations)

transform.reason: Confidence gating needs count-based support tests and a fallback prediction policy.

tools.definition: The number of sightings a window needs before its prediction is used; the knob that makes hierarchical N-grams work.

tools.title: Application in combat

transform.reason: Combat prediction needs a counter-action mapping and deliberate response throttling.

tools.definition: Use predicted attacks or dodges to counter the player, deliberately throttled so the opponent feels skilled rather than psychic.

tools.title: Decision learning

transform.reason: Decision learning needs observation encoding, target actions, and a learner update.

tools.definition: Learning a mapping from observed situation to chosen action, the inter-behaviour problem made tractable by fixing the set of actions and observations.

tools.title: The structure of decision learning

transform.reason: Training examples need an attribute schema, action labels, and collection rules.

tools.definition: Observations are encoded as a vector of attributes, actions as a fixed set, and examples pair the two, either from watching a player or from the outcome of the AI's own choices.

hooks.clause: a feedback example is a situation vector paired with the correction taken

tools.title: Supervised examples vs reward feedback

transform.reason: Feedback choices need distinct label-driven and reward-driven update contracts.

tools.definition: Learning from demonstrated decisions needs labelled examples and copies their flaws; learning from outcomes needs only a reward signal but learns slowly and can find odd strategies.

tools.title: What should you learn?

transform.reason: Bounded learning design needs a declared action set and informative observation criteria.

tools.definition: Choose the observations and actions deliberately: learn small, well-bounded choices with informative attributes, not the whole behaviour.

tools.title: Four techniques
tools.definition: The chapter's chosen decision learners: naive Bayes classification, decision tree learning, reinforcement learning and artificial neural networks.

tools.title: Naive Bayes classifier

transform.reason: Bayesian classification needs conditional counts, priors, smoothing, and class selection.

tools.definition: Predict the most probable action by multiplying, for each attribute, how often that attribute value accompanied each action, assuming attributes are independent given the action.

hooks.clause: classify incoming feedback into rule families from simple attribute counts

tools.title: Conditional independence assumption

transform.reason: Independence assumptions need an attribute model and a probabilistic evaluator.

tools.definition: Treating attributes as independent is wrong in general but makes the counts tiny and the classifier robust; it works surprisingly often.
